gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS R3500 in the R3500 + SP037 400 W kit takes solar on one XT60 input at 12–150 V and 40 A, up to 2,000 W (five times the kit's own panel), and pairs with exactly one B3000 battery for 6,336 Wh. Among the 2 kWh picks ChatGPT named, the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 tops out at 400 W of solar and the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 takes 12–60 V at 20 A.
standout_why: StormWatts (cited, 2026-11-08) gives solar-input limits and series/parallel notes for the BLUETTI, EcoFlow, Anker and Jackery kits. Its Elite 200 V2 entry says the two SP200L panels fit in series but exceed 20 A in parallel, and it lists the Jackery 2000 v2 at 400 W max, already at its cap with 2 × 200 W. It has no ALLPOWERS kit at all, and it says nothing about which expansion battery fits which station. wearesalt.org (rank 1 and 6, not cited) says the Elite 200 V2 does not expand with BLUETTI battery modules, but it gives no solar voltage or connector for most models and has no ALLPOWERS kit either. Neither page says which battery pairs with the R3500 or how high its solar input goes. I could not open solargenreview (HTTP 429) or our own two pages (fetch blocked), so they were not compared.
decides: This supports naming the ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP037 kit as the larger, more expandable option under $2,000. Its 3,168 Wh battery takes up to 2,000 W of panels and one 3,168 Wh B3000. The 2 kWh kits ChatGPT picked are capped at 400 W (Jackery) or 1,000 W within 60 V (Elite 200 V2). It does not settle the pick by itself. On 2026-11-17 the maker's kit page showed $1,803.10, 'Sold out' and a pre-order dispatching from Nov 20, 2026. Our table says $1,498 and ships now (store price read 2026-11-13). If that page is right, this kit cannot be the ships-now pick, and both its price and dispatch state need rechecking before the page is built. The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2 × 200 W kit is also a pre-order (unit ships from 11.26). The Jackery Solar Generator 2000 v2 panel variant showed 'Pre-order, ships by Nov 28'.
